official.title: Doctoral Researcher (Photoacoustic Aerosol and Black Carbon Measurements)
official.description_text:
Tampere University and Tampere University of Applied Sciences create a unique environment for multidisciplinary, inspirational and high-impact research and education. Our university community has its competitive edges in technology, health and society
.
www.tuni.fi/en
The Aerosol and Cloud Particle Optics group, part of the Aerosol Physics Laboratory at Tampere University, is establishing a new research direction in photoacoustic measurement technology within Tampere's strong aerosol research ecosystem. The group brings established expertise in photoacoustic and optical measurements, complemented by the Aerosol Physics Laboratory's long-standing expertise in aerosols and combustion processes. This work builds on monitoring-capable, multi-wavelength photoacoustic instrumentation, including PAAS-4λ, which has been operating at Hyytiälä since 2023.
Job description
As a doctoral researcher, you will carry out a focused research project on next-generation photoacoustic methods for aerosol and black-carbon measurements. Your core tasks will be to contribute to the development and construction of a new PAAS instrument version for laboratory testing and characterization, and to develop, test and validate new traceable calibration routines for photoacoustic and optical aerosol measurements. The work combines hands-on instrumentation, laboratory experiments, uncertainty analysis, programming and scientific data analysis.
A central motivation is Directive (EU) 2024/2881 on ambient air quality and cleaner air for Europe, which introduces black-carbon monitoring at urban and rural monitoring supersites. This creates a clear need for accurate, traceable and comparable optical measurements of equivalent black carbon (eBC).
As your expertise develops, you will have room to shape your own research questions. Possible directions include analysing existing data from sub-Arctic and Arctic regions, investigating how atmospheric processing changes the optical properties of black carbon, and developing ideas for future measurements.
Requirements
Applicants must hold an internationally recognized Master's degree in physics, engineering, aerosol or atmospheric science, optics, photonics, environmental science or another relevant field by the starting date. You should be motivated by experimental research, measurement technology and learning across disciplines.
The most important qualifications are hands-on experience with scientific instrumentation and strong programming and data-analysis skills in Python, MATLAB or comparable tools. Previous work with black-carbon or photoacoustic instruments is a significant advantage. Experience in aerosol measurements, optics, electronics, data acquisition, calibration or uncertainty analysis is also valuable. Excellent English and constructive teamwork are essential; Finnish is not required.
We offer
You will receive structured doctoral training and close scientific supervision while developing expertise in experimental aerosol science, optics and advanced measurement technology. You will work closely with the Postdoctoral Researcher recruited alongside this position and with experienced researchers in the group. As your project progresses, you will take increasing responsibility for experiments, analysis, publications and presentations at international conferences.
We offer a fixed-term Doctoral Researcher position for three years. The preferred starting date is 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible by mutual agreement. A trial period of six months applies to all our new employees. The salary will be based on both the job requirements and the employee's personal performance in accordance with the
Finnish University Salary System
. A typical starting salary for a Doctoral Researcher is around EUR 3,000 per month.
The Aerosol and Cloud Particle Optics group has a long record of developing optical instruments for aerosol and cloud research and an extensive network of international collaborators. At Tampere University, this expertise is embedded in the Aerosol Physics Laboratory, adding its strengths in aerosols, combustion processes and measurement technology to a strong interdisciplinary research environment.
As a member of staff at Tampere University, you will enjoy a range of competitive benefits, such as occupational health care services, flexible work schedule, versatile research infrastructure, modern teaching facilities and a safe and inviting campus area as well as a personal fund to spend on sports and cultural activities in your free time. www.tuni.fi
Tehtävänkuvaus
Tampereen yliopiston Aerosol and Cloud Particle Optics -tutkimusryhmä etsii väitöskirjatutkijaa kehittämään fotoakustista mittausteknologiaa aerosoli- ja mustan hiilen mittauksiin. Työhön kuuluu uuden PAAS-mittalaitteen version rakentaminen ja testaaminen sekä uusien jäljitettävien kalibrointimenetelmien kehittäminen.
Tutkimuksessa voidaan hyödyntää olemassa olevia subarktisilta ja arktisilta alueilta kerättyjä aineistoja sekä kehittää uusia mittausideoita. Ryhmän pitkä kokemus optisten mittalaitteiden kehittämisestä ja kansainvälisestä yhteistyöstä yhdistyy Aerosolifysiikan laboratorion vahvaan aerosoli-, polttoprosessi- ja mittausteknologiaosaamiseen.
Tehtävä täytetään kolmeksi vuodeksi. Toivottu aloitusajankohta on 1.1.2027 tai mahdollisimman pian sopimuksen mukaan.
Edellytykset
Hakijalla tulee olla soveltuva ylempi korkeakoulututkinto, sujuva englannin kielen taito, käytännön instrumentointiosaamista ja hyvät ohjelmointitaidot. Kokemus mustan hiilen tai fotoakustisista mittalaitteista katsotaan erityiseksi eduksi.
Hakijan tulee pystyä työskentelemään yhteistyössä kansainvälisessä ja monitieteisessä tutkimusympäristössä.
Hakuohjeet
Lue tarkemmat tiedot tehtävästä ja hakuohjeet yllä olevasta englanninkielisestä ilmoituksesta.
Jätäthän hakemuksesi yliopiston sähköisellä hakulomakkeella (linkki löytyy tämän ilmoituksen alta).
Hakuaika tehtävään päättyy 18.10.2026.

ai.summary: Tampere University is recruiting a doctoral researcher to develop photoacoustic measurement technology for aerosol and black-carbon monitoring. The work combines hands-on instrumentation design, laboratory experimentation, calibration, programming, and data analysis within an atmospheric measurement science context.

thematic_fit.rationale: This position is in experimental measurement technology and atmospheric science, not immersive systems or HCI. The researcher's domains (spatial learning, collaborative systems, wayfinding, multiplayer interaction) do not intersect with photoacoustic instrumentation or aerosol physics. The position's core is scientific instrumentation and environmental monitoring—purely technical and domain-specific to atmospheric measurement.

methodological_fit.rationale: The researcher has intermediate experimental design, quantitative research, and programming skills. This position requires hands-on instrumentation work, programming in Python/MATLAB, experimental design, calibration, and uncertainty analysis. These methodological elements overlap: the researcher has conducted user studies and data analysis. However, the context is entirely different—the researcher studied human spatial cognition and learning outcomes in immersive environments, not physical measurement systems. The experimental rigor transfers, but the domain-specific knowledge (aerosol physics, optics, calibration protocols) must be learned from scratch.

growth_value.rationale: This position would develop strong experimental design, rigorous measurement methodology, and advanced programming skills (Python/MATLAB). The researcher would gain expertise in instrumentation, calibration, and uncertainty quantification—valuable for any empirical researcher. However, these capabilities do not advance the target goal of designing human-centred immersive systems. The researcher would become an atmospheric measurement scientist rather than an HCI researcher.

strategic_value.rationale: Tampere University is in the researcher's Priority 2 target list and Finland is a preferred country. The group has established expertise and is building new research directions. Funding is secure via EU and Finnish research councils. However, the research direction (photoacoustic aerosol measurement) is orthogonal to the researcher's target identity (human-centred XR). A PhD here would be in environmental measurement science, not immersive systems research. After graduation, the researcher would have credentials in aerosol science, making it harder to transition to HCI or XR research.

eligibility_flags: Requires MSc in physics, engineering, aerosol/atmospheric science, optics, photonics, environmental science or 'another relevant field' by start date. The researcher's MSc is in multimedia/creative technology—while interdisciplinary, it may not be considered 'relevant' by the atmospheric science department. Direct contact with Martin Schnaiter or Emma Järvinen is essential to clarify eligibility.
Doctoral researcher position requires start date 1 Jan 2027 or ASAP. The researcher's MSc is in thesis stage; confirm defence/conferment timeline against this deadline.
risks: Domain mismatch: The researcher would be trained as an atmospheric measurement scientist, not an HCI researcher. This PhD would further entrench a technical/instrumentation specialization rather than advancing the target goal of human-centred design research.

Limited methodological transfer: While experimental design skills transfer, the specific instrumentation and domain expertise (photoacoustic optics, aerosol physics) do not support immersive systems research.

Competitive disadvantage: The researcher would compete against candidates with physics, engineering, or atmospheric science backgrounds. An MSc in multimedia/creative technology may be seen as unconventional or insufficiently rigorous in a measurement science context.

Career path divergence: After this PhD, the researcher would hold credentials in atmospheric measurement science. Transitioning to HCI/XR research at a postdoc level would require explaining a significant career pivot and might face skepticism from HCI groups who would question why they were recruited into measurement science.
